tier_reason: The perf page has BenchmarkDotNet tables comparing Nino against MessagePack-CSharp and MemoryPack. The Ratio column gives 13.68 (MessagePack) and 2.44 (MemoryPack) for SimpleClass serialize, 5.17 and 1.90 for deserialize, and 52.05 and 1.29 for SimpleStruct serialize. The environment block states .NET 9.0.0 Arm64 RyuJIT AdvSIMD, BenchmarkDotNet v0.14.0 ShortRun (a Release build), and an Apple M1 CPU. The harness is public in src/Nino.Benchmark/SimpleTest.cs, with the same method names, ShortRunJob(Net90) and payload column, plus SimpleBenchmarkData.cs and Program.cs, so this stays A.

corrections.baseline: MessagePack (MessagePack-CSharp, NuGet package 'MessagePack'); MemoryPack also compared
corrections.workload: BenchmarkDotNet micro-benchmarks timing serialize and deserialize separately (not a round trip). Serialize writes into a reused buffer writer. Payloads: one SimpleClass (int, bool, Guid, DateTime, two strings, int[100], List<DateTime>(10), two 10-entry Dictionary<int,...>), one SimpleStruct (int + DateTime), arrays of 100 of each, and a 10,000-element Vector4[]
corrections.compiler_and_flags: .NET 9.0.0 (9.0.24.52809) Arm64 RyuJIT AdvSIMD; .NET SDK 9.0.101 (host .NET 8.0.6); BenchmarkDotNet v0.14.0 ShortRun job (3 iterations, 1 launch, 3 warmups), Release build (csproj Optimize=true), GcServer(true)
corrections.caveats: First-party results on the project's docs site. The page is undated and gives no package versions. From its BenchmarkDotNet 0.14.0 header and Vectors rows it was made with a 2025 harness revision (Feb-Jul 2025, when the csproj pinned MessagePack 3.1.3 and MemoryPack 1.21.4). Current main uses BenchmarkDotNet 0.15.2 and MessagePack 3.1.7, so a re-run may differ. The ShortRun job (3 iterations) is statistically light. The struct rows are near the timer floor (Nino SimpleStruct deserialize 0.39 ns, serialize 2.82 ns), so the 52x/120x struct ratios mean little; the SimpleClass ratios (13.68x/5.17x vs MessagePack) are the meaningful ones. MemoryPack ties Nino on Vector4[] (ratio 0.99 on deserialize, 1.01 on serialize).

notes: The claimed ratios match the page exactly. The page also shows 12.92x/3.25x (serialize/deserialize) over MessagePack for arrays of 100 SimpleClass. Repo metadata is correct: MIT, not a fork, 649 stars, last commit 2026-06-12, active.

tier_reason: Upgrade from B. GLD.SerializerBenchmark publishes the harness: zig/src/extra.zig (encodeS2s/decodeS2s), zig/src/proto_ser.zig, zig/src/runner.zig and zig/scripts/run-benchmarks.sh, which builds with 'zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast'. It also publishes the run's environment in dashboard/public/data/zig_latest.json.gz: Zig 0.16.0 and a 12th Gen Intel Core i7-12800H. The run's dirty tree only held the dependency-pin bump committed with the data (4a51f66e). So code, compiler, flags and CPU model are all public for the s2s-vs-protobuf comparison.

corrections.baseline: Protocol Buffers (Arwalk/zig-protobuf 5.0.0, generated from the suite's shared benchmark_v2.proto); MessagePack (serde.zig 1.2.1 backend) also compared
corrections.claimed_speedup: Serialize+deserialize time in run 2026-09-14-134825, 100-instance cells: 1.13-1.99x faster than zig-protobuf on all 5 fixtures in stream mode over all trials (document 1.88x, event 1.43x, message 1.43x, strings 1.13x, telemetry 1.99x). With bytes mode and the dashboard's default IQR filter it is 1.12-2.02x, and single-instance cells give 1.21-2.09x. Against serde.zig's MessagePack backend: 1.4-2.2x faster on 4 of 5 fixtures, slower on strings (0.92x). (all derived from page data) The Cap'n Proto '12.9-17.9x' figure is dropped: that row calls the C++ runtime through a C bridge compiled with no -O flag.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Zig 0.16.0, zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast (zig/scripts/run-benchmarks.sh); the Cap'n Proto C bridge is built by system c++ (g++ 11.4) with no -O flag
corrections.hardware: 12th Gen Intel Core i7-12800H (20 logical cores, powersave governor), 32 GB RAM, Ubuntu 22.04, Linux 6.8.0-138
corrections.workload: Serialize+deserialize time on 5 shared fixtures (document, event, message, strings, telemetry) from the suite's common IDLs. Single-instance and 100-instance cells, bytes and stream modes, 100 reps per cell with 1 warmup, in the GLD.SerializerBenchmark Zig runner
corrections.caveats: Third-party suite, but not a well-known one: the repo dates from 2015 (not first published 2026-09), has 25 stars, and added its Zig runner on 2026-08-29. This was a single-session run (the suite's own claim level L1) on a laptop CPU under the powersave governor. Protobuf's timed decode also converts the generated message back into the suite struct, while s2s decodes straight into it. s2s payloads are about 1.1-1.7x larger than protobuf's, and s2s serialize is slower than protobuf's on 'strings'. s2s loses to zig-flatbuffers on strings and telemetry, to msgpack.zig on strings (about a tie elsewhere), and to the suite's in-tree comptime-bin encoder on every fixture. The Cap'n Proto row is not a fair baseline because of the unoptimized C bridge and extra copies. s2s is a Zig-only format; its README calls it complete only for the 'trivial' case.

notes: The record's ratios do appear in the data file, but only for one unstated slice (100-instance, stream mode, all trials); I made the claim explicit and dropped the Cap'n Proto comparison because of the -O0 bridge. The record gave hardware as null, but zig_latest.json.gz has the CPU model, so I upgraded to A. The serde.msgpack adapter path changed after this run (#167), so that secondary comparison may shift on the next run. The s2s and protobuf paths have not changed since.

tier_reason: The README Speed section is a first-party benchy table comparing flatty against Nim's std/marshal (plus bingo, frosty and jsony). The code is public in tests/bench.nim, but no compiler version, flags or hardware are given; tests/config.nims only sets --path. The deserialize min-time gap is over 50x with flags unstated, so C is also the cap.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Serialize min time: 2.265 ms vs 85.178 ms for std/marshal (~37.6x); avg 2.413 vs 93.228 ms (~38.6x). Deserialize min time: 2.643 ms vs 148.723 ms (~56.3x); avg 4.285 vs 155.663 ms (~36.3x). (derived from page data)
corrections.workload: Serialize and deserialize an 11,125-node ref-object tree (bool, int, 3 strings, uint16[32], uint64[16] and a child seq per node), 100 runs each with benchy timeIt; std/marshal serializes to JSON text
corrections.caveats: The baseline is Nim's std/marshal, whose format is JSON, so this compares a binary format against a JSON-text serializer. It is not one of the category's named baselines (Protobuf/FlatBuffers/Cap'n Proto/MessagePack). Among binary peers, bingo is only ~16% slower on serialize (2.632 vs 2.265 ms min). No hardware, compiler or flags are stated. The std/marshal row was added on 2026-05-25. The benchmark code is public in tests/bench.nim. flatty has no versioning, per its README.

notes: The numbers match the README exactly. The record's ratios use the min-time column; with average times the deserialize gap is ~36x, not 56x. Repo metadata is correct: MIT, not a fork, 95 stars, last commit 2026-08-13, active.
